cards.statement: WebP supports alpha-channel transparency alongside lossy image compression.
cards.explanation: Lossy WebP can preserve an alpha channel, so a transparent image does not require lossless encoding.

cards.statement: MDN describes AVIF images as displaying progressively during download.
cards.explanation: MDN describes AVIF rendering as waiting for the complete file, rather than showing increasingly detailed partial downloads.
cards.misconception: AVIF behaves like a progressive JPEG during download.
cards.appliesTo: MDN Web Docs AVIF rendering guidance, checked 2026-10-04
cards.volatilityNote: MDN's rendering guidance may change as browser AVIF decoders evolve.

source.title: Image file type and format guide

cards.statement: MDN describes PNG compression as retaining the pixel information encoded in the image.
cards.explanation: PNG compression retains the pixel data it encodes; reducing file size through compression does not discard that information.

source.title: Image file type and format guide

cards.statement: The browser selects the smallest supported-format file among a picture element's sources.
cards.explanation: A picture element uses the first source whose type and media conditions match. It does not compare the file sizes of matching sources.
cards.misconception: The browser chooses among picture sources by comparing download sizes.

cards.statement: A srcset width descriptor states the candidate image's intrinsic pixel width.
cards.explanation: A width descriptor describes the image file's intrinsic width, giving the browser information for responsive image selection.

cards.statement: Omitting sizes makes the browser infer a srcset source size from the image's CSS width.
cards.explanation: For width-descriptor selection, an omitted sizes attribute defaults to 100vw, the viewport width, rather than the image's computed CSS width.
cards.misconception: The browser measures the CSS layout width when sizes is omitted.

cards.statement: With width descriptors in srcset, the browser adds src as a 1x image candidate.
cards.explanation: With density descriptors, src can supply a 1x candidate; width-based srcset makes the browser ignore src.
cards.misconception: src enters the candidate set regardless of descriptor type.

cards.statement: decoding="async" hints that the browser can paint other content ahead of image decoding.
cards.explanation: Asynchronous decoding expresses a preference to present other content first, rather than hold its next paint for the image to decode.

cards.statement: The browser applies loading="lazy" to ordinary img elements by default.
cards.explanation: An img element defaults to eager loading, which fetches the image regardless of its distance from the viewport.
cards.misconception: Native image loading automatically defers offscreen images.

source.title: Browser-level image lazy loading for the web

cards.statement: The browser waits for layout to locate an image before applying loading="lazy".
cards.explanation: Native image lazy loading needs the image's layout position to decide when its request should begin.

source.title: Lazy load images and iframe elements

cards.statement: Native image lazy loading can defer requests while the browser's JavaScript setting is disabled.
cards.explanation: Browsers defer native lazy-image requests only when JavaScript is enabled; disabling scripting preserves ordinary image loading.
cards.misconception: Native deferral works identically with scripting enabled or disabled.

cards.statement: A page uses an interactive placeholder to postpone a heavy third-party embed until user engagement.
cards.explanation: An embed facade substitutes lightweight content, then loads the full embed when the user engages with it.

source.title: Lazy load images and iframe elements

cards.statement: The browser discovers a font URL in external CSS after it downloads and parses that stylesheet.
cards.explanation: A font URL inside an external stylesheet sits behind the stylesheet request and parsing, making font discovery later than HTML resource discovery.

cards.statement: During the font block period, the browser removes the waiting text from layout calculations.
cards.explanation: During the block period, the browser lays out text using an invisible fallback font; the text still occupies space.
cards.misconception: Invisible text during font loading has no layout footprint.

source.title: CSS Fonts Module Level 4: Font Display Timeline

cards.statement: MDN describes font-display: swap as using visible fallback while the browser awaits a web font.
cards.explanation: The swap strategy has a minimal block period, then presents fallback text while the requested face becomes available.

cards.statement: The browser treats font-display: auto as an explicit request for the block strategy.
cards.explanation: font-display: auto delegates the display strategy to the user agent, rather than selecting the block strategy explicitly.
cards.misconception: auto explicitly selects block behavior.

cards.statement: font-display: optional can replace visible fallback text with a web font that arrives late.
cards.explanation: The optional strategy has no swap period. A font that misses its brief block period leaves the fallback in use for that visit.
cards.misconception: optional permits a late replacement after fallback text appears.

cards.statement: WOFF2 uses Brotli compression to reduce the amount of font data a browser downloads.
cards.explanation: Brotli compression helps WOFF2 deliver font data in smaller files than WOFF, reducing transfer work.

cards.statement: Preloading a font requires crossorigin even when the font URL shares the page's origin.
cards.explanation: Font fetches use CORS mode. The preload needs crossorigin to match that mode even for a font served from the same origin.

cards.statement: The browser starts a font download when it first parses that font's @font-face declaration.
cards.explanation: An @font-face declaration alone does not request its file; normal CSS font loading starts when page styling uses the face.
cards.misconception: Declaring a font face starts its download immediately.

cards.statement: web.dev recommends comparing transfer times when evaluating self-hosted and third-party fonts.
cards.explanation: web.dev recommends comparing font transfer time, including connection setup; hosting infrastructure affects the result.

cards.statement: unicode-range lets the browser fetch matching glyphs as a partial font file.
cards.explanation: unicode-range controls whether a font face is needed. A matching character triggers the whole file; separate subset files provide the byte savings.
cards.misconception: The descriptor makes the browser download part of an individual font file.

cards.statement: size-adjust scales a font face's glyph outlines and associated metrics together.
cards.explanation: The size-adjust multiplier scales glyph shapes and metrics, helping align fallback typography with a chosen web font.

cards.statement: line-gap-override replaces the CSS line-height value on elements using that font.
cards.explanation: line-gap-override changes the font face's line-gap metric used in line layout; it does not replace an element's CSS line-height declaration.
cards.misconception: A font metric descriptor overwrites an element's line-height declaration.

cards.statement: Cache-Control: private restricts response storage to private caches such as the browser's cache.
cards.explanation: The private directive permits browser-cache storage while excluding shared caches; it defines where a response is cacheable.

source.title: Prevent unnecessary network requests with the HTTP Cache

cards.statement: A response's max-age freshness period starts when the browser receives the response.
cards.explanation: max-age counts from response generation at the origin. An Age header reduces the freshness time remaining when the browser receives it.
cards.misconception: Receipt by the browser restarts the freshness clock.

cards.statement: A shared cache uses s-maxage ahead of max-age when a response carries both directives.
cards.explanation: s-maxage overrides max-age for shared-cache freshness, letting servers give shared caches a separate lifetime.

cards.statement: A cache treats Cache-Control: no-cache as a ban on storing the response.
cards.explanation: no-cache permits storage but requires validation before reuse; it controls reuse rather than forbidding storage.
cards.misconception: no-cache prohibits storage instead of requiring revalidation.

cards.statement: The must-revalidate directive triggers validation while the cached response remains fresh.
cards.explanation: must-revalidate permits reuse while a response is fresh. Once stale, the cache must validate it before reuse.
cards.misconception: must-revalidate forces validation even during freshness.

cards.statement: A server responds with 304 when a conditional GET's If-None-Match matches the current ETag.
cards.explanation: For an unchanged representation, the server sends 304 Not Modified with no body, allowing the client to reuse its stored response.

cards.statement: stale-while-revalidate allows a cache to reuse a stale response within its extra window.
cards.explanation: Within that additional window, a cache can serve stale content while it revalidates in the background, hiding the validation wait.

cards.statement: Updating a versioned asset on the server makes the browser refresh its still-fresh cached copy.
cards.explanation: A still-fresh asset can remain in the HTTP cache after the server changes it; a new versioned URL makes the browser request the new asset.
cards.misconception: Changing server bytes invalidates a browser's fresh cached asset.

source.title: Prevent unnecessary network requests with the HTTP Cache

cards.statement: Vary: Accept-Encoding adds the request's Accept-Encoding value to cache variant selection.
cards.explanation: A cache distinguishes responses using the named request header, preventing reuse of a variant for an incompatible encoding preference.

cards.statement: Content-Encoding lets the client advertise the compression formats it accepts.
cards.explanation: Content-Encoding identifies the coding applied to a representation. Accept-Encoding communicates the client's acceptable codings.
cards.misconception: Content-Encoding advertises the client's decoding preferences.

cards.statement: A gzip response's Content-Length describes the body's byte count after decompression.
cards.explanation: For an encoded body, Content-Length refers to the encoded bytes sent, rather than the larger decoded representation.
cards.misconception: Content-Length reports the size of the original uncompressed content.

cards.statement: Transfer-Encoding describes message transfer between neighboring HTTP nodes.
cards.explanation: Transfer-Encoding applies to an individual network hop, so intermediaries may use different transfer encodings on successive hops.

cards.statement: The browser reconstructs a page's JavaScript heap during a bfcache restore.
cards.explanation: A bfcache restore resumes the saved document and JavaScript heap instead of rebuilding the runtime from cached resource files.
cards.misconception: A bfcache restore recreates the document's runtime.

cards.statement: The browser sets pageshow.persisted to true when it restores a page from the bfcache.
cards.explanation: The persisted flag on pageshow distinguishes a restored document from an ordinary page load.

cards.statement: pagehide.persisted=true confirms successful bfcache storage by the browser.
cards.explanation: pagehide.persisted=true signals an intent to cache the page, rather than a guarantee of a later restore.
cards.misconception: Intent to cache guarantees a future restore.

cards.statement: web.dev recommends pagehide in place of unload for page-exit handling.
cards.explanation: web.dev advises avoiding unload and using pagehide for exit handling, including bfcache transitions.

cards.statement: MDN recommends keeping a beforeunload listener after the user saves pending edits.
cards.explanation: MDN recommends attaching beforeunload while unsaved changes exist and removing the listener when that warning is no longer needed.
cards.misconception: A permanent beforeunload listener is recommended for saved pages.

cards.statement: Keeping window.opener lets both linked pages enter the bfcache independently.
cards.explanation: web.dev identifies live opener references as a bfcache obstacle because other windows may access the cached window.
cards.misconception: Linked windows remain independently eligible for bfcache.
cards.appliesTo: bfcache eligibility described by web.dev, checked 2026-10-04
cards.volatilityNote: Browser bfcache eligibility rules for linked windows can evolve.

cards.statement: In Chrome, a page served with Cache-Control: no-store can qualify for the bfcache.
cards.explanation: Chrome permits no-store pages under extra restrictions and evicts them when cookies or other authorization methods change.
cards.appliesTo: Chrome following the March-April 2025 rollout, checked 2026-10-04
cards.volatilityNote: Chrome's eligibility restrictions and eviction conditions for no-store pages can change.

cards.statement: Chrome exposes cross-origin iframe blocking details through its notRestoredReasons API.
cards.explanation: For cross-origin frames, Chrome masks the detailed reasons; the top-level report can include a masked reason instead.
cards.misconception: The parent page receives cross-origin iframe diagnostics in full.
cards.volatilityNote: Browser support and the details exposed by notRestoredReasons can change.

cards.statement: Chrome DevTools tests bfcache restoration by navigating away from a page and back.
cards.explanation: The DevTools test performs a round trip and reports whether the page was restored from bfcache, with diagnostics for failures.

cards.statement: web.dev recommends resetting INP to zero when a page returns from the bfcache.
cards.explanation: A restore begins a distinct visit for INP measurement, so earlier interaction latencies should not carry into the restored visit.

cards.statement: freeze and resume are Baseline lifecycle events across major browser engines.
cards.explanation: freeze and resume remain Chromium-specific lifecycle events, rather than Baseline features.
cards.misconception: The lifecycle events have cross-engine Baseline availability.
cards.appliesTo: Chromium browsers; Chrome 68 and later, checked 2026-10-04
cards.volatilityNote: freeze and resume support may expand to other browser engines.

cards.statement: web.dev measures LCP after a bfcache restore from pageshow to the next painted frame.
cards.explanation: Restore LCP is the time until that next frame paints; FCP has the same value on a bfcache restore.
